title: Gas Power Plant Commissioning Logistics
fullBody:
## Project Overview

A major energy developer commissioned SSVT Logistics to manage the complete logistics for a new 450 MW gas-fired power plant in Maharashtra, India. The project involved importing and installing two gas turbine generators, one steam turbine, six heat recovery steam generators, and associated electrical and control equipment from manufacturers in Europe, Japan, and the United States.

## Key Logistics Challenges

The gas turbine generators — at 320 tonnes each — were the heaviest and most critical items. These precision pieces of rotating equipment required specialist transport, careful handling to avoid vibration damage, and protected storage at site prior to installation.

The project site was 65 kilometres from the nearest port capable of handling heavy lift vessels, requiring a road transport solution through semi-urban roads with numerous overhead utility lines and bridge crossings.

## Our Approach

SSVT appointed a dedicated project director who interfaced directly with the client's project management team from the contract award. A detailed logistics execution plan was developed covering each equipment item from factory to installation pad.

For the gas turbines, we designed a specialist transport solution using a 24-axle SPMT configuration capable of carrying the 320-tonne loads. The 65-kilometre road route was prepared over three weeks including bridge inspections, utility lift arrangements, and road resurfacing at the approach to one critical bridge.

All electrical and control equipment was transported in climate-controlled containers to protect sensitive electronics from temperature and humidity extremes during the sea voyage from Europe and Japan.

## Outcome

Both gas turbines were delivered to site and positioned on their foundations within the project programme. The steam turbine and all ancillary equipment were delivered on schedule. The plant achieved first fire on the target date, and SSVT received commendation from the client for logistics execution quality and safety performance.
outcome: 450 MW power plant equipment delivered on schedule. Both 320-tonne gas turbines positioned on foundations without incident. Plant achieved first fire on target date.
